description: Verify that DUT replies to an ARP Request where target_hw equals DUT's own MAC and the Ethernet destination is broadcast — the most common shape of a real ARP Request (RFC 826 §2.4)
approach:
[Objective]
This is the textbook shape of an ARP Request: target_hw filled with the (already known to be) DUT MAC and Ethernet destination set to broadcast so any host can read it. DUT must reply because target_ip matches.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ARP Request injected
   • opcode       = 1
   • eth_dst      = ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff   (broadcast)
   • target_hw    = DUT iface MAC
   • target_ip    = DUT IP
   • sender_*     = HOST-1-IP / MAC-ADDR1

2. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: ARP Reply (opcode 2, sender_mac=DUT, target_ip=HOST-1-IP)

[Pass condition]
DUT emits an ARP Reply within the observation window.

[Fail condition]
Fail_no_reply — DUT did not reply. This is the most common ARP shape; failure here indicates a fundamental reception bug.

verdicts.Pass: DUT replied to a textbook-shape ARP Request — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_reply: DUT did not reply to the most common ARP Request shape — fundamental reception bug
